subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Charlie Nguyen <charlie.nguyen@acme-media.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

Hi Charlie / Priya —

Thanks for the call today — good sync. Per our discussion, I wanted to capture the key SLOs and next steps so we can get the customer-led load test scheduled:

SLOs discussed (target):
- Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms for single-stream text generation (500 token max).
- Throughput: sustain ~120 requests/sec for 8k tokens/day average; burst to 400 rps for short windows.
- Concurrency: support 200 concurrent sessions with KV cache enabled; scale to 500 for peak bursts.
- Streaming: chunked/streaming responses required for chat UX (server should support chunked responses / SSE or chunked HTTP) — partial tokens must arrive within 200ms once generation starts.

Load test approach: customer-led run using k6 (we also support Locust if you prefer). We will provide:
- a test account + API key scoped to load-testing (no PII)
- a sample k6 script (attached) you can modify to mirror your traffic patterns
- an IP allowlist template to give to your infra team
- a short runbook and monitoring checklist (attached)

Proposed test window: Thu 2026-03-05 18:00–20:00 PST (we can shift earlier if that works better for you). Please confirm preferred window and whether you want k6 or Locust.

Next steps / action owners:
- Charlie / Priya: confirm test window and tool (k6/Locust) — ACTION: reply by EOD Wed
- Dev (solutions eng): will provision test API key + create test project, share endpoints and token scopes
- Marissa (me): coordinate IP allowlist and runbook; stand by during test for escalation
- Aditya: will finalize MLP/contract notes if we see scaling beyond dedicated tier

Attachments: acme_k6_script_v1.js, loadtest_runbook.pdf, ip_allowlist_template.txt

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Charlie Nguyen <charlie.nguyen@acme-media.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-media.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Tooling: we have an existing k6 pipeline but our infra team prefers Locust for more complex user flows. Can you confirm Redwood supports Locust?

2) Concurrency: that 200 concurrent sessions is for standard chat flows (1–2 prompts/sec per session). For a small subset of users (premium tier) we may require 800 concurrent sessions during the promo burst. Can we test to 800 for a 10m ramp?

3) Streaming: yes streaming is required. We do incremental UI rendering and need the first tokens to arrive within 200ms. Also ask: does your streaming endpoint support chunked transfer-encoding and reconnect semantics if a connection drops?

4) IP allowlist: infra wants a full CIDR range to send to our firewall team. We’ll need this by Wed EOD.

We can take the Locust option if Redwood can run with it. Proposed window is still Thu 18:00–20:00 PST but we can move to 16:00–18:00 if you prefer earlier ops hours.

If you can confirm support for Locust and the 800 concurrent burst test, we’ll lock the window and get procurement looped in.

—
Charlie
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Media
charlie.nguyen@acme-media.com

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Charlie Nguyen <charlie.nguyen@acme-media.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-media.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

Hi Charlie / Priya —

Short answers: yes to Locust; yes to chunked streaming; yes we can support an 800 concurrent session burst for a short window but want to stage it. Details below.

1) Locust vs k6: Redwood exposes a standard HTTP/HTTPS API endpoint for inference. Locust scripts that issue concurrent HTTP POSTs to our /v1/generate endpoint will work fine. We recommend starting with k6 for baseline (lighter, deterministic), then run a Locust scenario for high-fidelity user flows. If you prefer, we can validate your Locustfile before the run.

2) Streaming: we support chunked transfer-encoding and server-sent events for streaming responses. Important notes:
   - First chunk latency depends on model and prompt length; for the models we discussed we typically see first-token p50 ~85ms, p95 ~300ms under moderate load.
   - When concurrency approaches max, latency increases non-linearly — we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts to mimic production.
   - For reconnect semantics: a resumed request will not continue token generation server-side; client should retry with last-received token as prefix (we can provide guidance in the runbook).

3) 800 concurrency burst: we can support it if you run a staged ramp: 0–200 (5m), 200–500 (5m), 500–800 (10m), hold 10m, then ramp down. This reduces cache churn and gives us a chance to observe tail latency. If you want an open blast to 800 immediate, we can run it but will flag higher error rates.

4) Test accounts / API key: I will provision a scoped API key that is rate-limited to the test project and audit-logged. Token will be for dev/test only; production keys will not be used. Expect the API key by Wed 12:00 PST.

5) IP allowlist: attached template filled with Redwood egress ranges. Please have your infra ops add these to your firewall. We will also coordinate with our infra team for any peering we need to enable.

6) Metrics to capture on your side: p50/p95 latency, error rate (4xx/5xx), successful token throughput, connection drops, and end-to-end UI render time. We’ll provide a Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint and Grafana dashboard link for the test.

Attachments: ip_allowlist_template.txt (filled), preliminary runbook snippet.

I’ll follow up with the API key + endpoints shortly.

—
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

Thanks Dev / Charlie —

We’re aligned on approach. Quick summary and final asks so procurement can proceed:
- Test window: Thu 2026-03-05 16:00–18:00 PST (Charlie requested earlier ops hours; greenlit)
- Load profile: baseline 200 concurrent, staged ramp to 800 for a 10m hold (Dev suggested ramp plan)
- Tool: Locust preferred by Acme — Dev will validate Locustfile 
- Streaming: Redwood supports chunked streaming + reconnect guidance in runbook

ACTION ITEMS: 
- Dev: share test API key + endpoints by Wed 12:00 PST (as mentioned) — Dev to include token scopes and expected per-key rate limits
- Charlie: confirm firewall allowlist acceptance and share any additional CIDRs we should include — Charlie to confirm by Wed EOD
- Priya / Procurement: we need a short procurement note for a 2-hour test (possible overage acceptance) — please loop procurement@acme-media.com

I’ll be on standby during the run and will coordinate our on-call infra if needed.

—
Marissa

From: Charlie Nguyen <charlie.nguyen@acme-media.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme-media.com>, procurement@acme-media.com
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

All right — procurement looped in. We accept the ramp plan. Two small asks before Wed 12:00 PST:

1) Please include in the API key email the exact header name and any special query params needed for streaming.
2) We need the full set of Redwood egress CIDRs (not just single IPs) for our firewall team. If you can paste them directly into the ip_allowlist_template we’ll forward to our ops.

We’ll plan to run Locust using the following scenario: 70% chat-stream flows (streaming enabled), 20% short-completion flows (non-streaming), 10% embeddings. Dev — can you validate embedding endpoint rate limits as well in the token you’ll provide?

—
Charlie

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Charlie Nguyen <charlie.nguyen@acme-media.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Mar 2026 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Performance SLOs & customer-led load test coordination

Charlie/Marissa —

Provisioned and sent: test project "acme-loadtest-2026-03" with scoped API key (sent to Charlie via secure link). Key details:
- Header: Authorization: Bearer <TEST_KEY>
- Streaming: use Accept: text/event-stream or chunked transfer; no extra query params required
- Embeddings endpoint: /v1/embeddings — test key rate-limited to 150 rps; generation endpoint test key rate-limited to 500 rps default but we can temporarily raise for the staged ramp to 1200 rps during the hold period (done for this test).
- Egress ranges: added full CIDR list into the ip_allowlist_template.txt attachment (see entry "Redwood-Egress-CIDRs")

I also uploaded a validated Locustfile to the Drive folder (linked in related_links) and a short checklist for reconnect semantics. I’ll be on call Thu 15:45 PST to help with any immediate troubleshooting.

If anything else comes up, ping me in the thread or DM.

—
Dev
